title: ISO 15552-style tie-rod pneumatic cylinder, 32 x 100
one_line: A double-acting, cushioned 32 mm bore tie-rod air cylinder with a 100 mm stroke, a rear double-clevis mount and a rod-end clevis. Every seal, bushing, nut, pin and circlip is its own solid, and the rod moves on one slider mate.
specs: Bore 32 mm, stroke 100 mm, piston rod 12 mm
Body length 94 mm + stroke (194 mm), end caps 45 mm square
4 x M6 tie rods on a 32.5 mm square, nuts at the front
G1/8 ports (8.8 mm tap-drill bores with feed passages) and slotted cushion needle screws in both caps
Piston: 2 back-to-back U-cup seals, wear band, magnet ring, rear cushion spear; front cushion collar on the rod
Rod gland: U-cup rod seal, bronze bushing, wiper
Rod end M10x1.25 x 22 with jam nut and ISO 8140-style clevis, 10 mm pin and 2 circlips
Rear double clevis (26 mm slot) on 4 x M6 socket screws, 10 mm pin and 2 circlips
Computed areas: piston 804.2 mm², rod-side annulus 691.2 mm²
parameters: stroke (length, 0-100 mm, clamped in the slider's distance expression; saved at 10 mm)
interference: 85 pairs, 0 interferences (stroke 10, 90 and 100 mm; 88 pairs, 0 interferences at 0 mm)
poses: stroke = 10 mm: assembly solve converged, 0 dof, 25/25 mates well
stroke = 90 mm: assembly solve converged, 0 dof, 25/25 mates well (hero.png and detail.png show this pose)
not_verified: Threads are not modelled (ports, tie rods, rod end, screws, piston-to-rod)
Seals are rigid sections just short of contact: no squeeze or sealing check
Cushioning is geometric only: no air flow, cushioning, force or pressure calculation
No materials or masses assigned; no force, pressure rating or mass is claimed
Clevis pins are fastened, not free revolutes; the rod does not turn about its axis
The tie-rod and mount-screw threads in the rear cap are simplified (they share holes, 1 mm apart)
